topics.title: Recognize there are cause-and-effect relationships related to matter and energy

subtopics.title: Recognize there are cause-and-effect relationships related to matter and energy (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Use senses to explore the properties of objects and materials (e.g., solids, liquids).
Make simple observations, predictions, explanations, and generalizations based on real-life experiences.
Collect, describe, predict and record information using words, drawings, maps, graphs and charts.
Observe, describe, and discuss living things and natural processes.

subtopics.title: Recognize there are cause-and-effect relationships related to matter and energy (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Recognize and investigate cause-and-effect relationships in everyday experiences (pushing, pulling, kicking, rolling or blowing objects).
Notice change in matter.
Observe, describe and discuss properties of materials and transformation of substances.
Seek answers to questions and test predictions using simple experiments.

topics.title: Recognize that living things have unique characteristics and basic needs that can be observed and studied

subtopics.title: Recognize that living things have unique characteristics and basic needs that can be observed and studied

outcomes.text: Observe, describe and discuss living things.
Observe similarities and differences in the needs of living things.
Observe and describe how natural habitats provide for the basic needs of plants and animals with respect to shelter, food, water, air and light.
Ask and pursue questions through simple investigations and observations of living things.
Collect, describe, and record information about living things through discussion, drawings, graphs, technology and charts.
Identify differences between living and nonliving things.

topics.title: Recognize that living things develop in predictable patterns

subtopics.title: Recognize that living things develop in predictable patterns

outcomes.text: Identify the common needs such as food, air and water of familiar living things.
Predict, explain and infer patterns based on observations and representations of living things, their needs and life cycles.
Observe and document changes in living things over time using different modalities such as drawing, dramatization, describing or using technology.
Recognize that plants and animals grow and change.

topics.title: The acquisition of concepts and facts related to the Earth materials and their uses

subtopics.title: The acquisition of concepts and facts related to the Earth materials and their uses

outcomes.text: Use senses and tools, including technology, to investigate materials, and observe processes and relationships to gather information and explore the environment.
Inquire about the natural and physical environment.
Observe and discuss common properties, differences and comparisons among objects.
Participate in simple investigations to form hypothesis, gather observations, draw conclusions.
Record observations using words, drawings, maps, graphs and charts.

topics.title: The acquisition of concepts and facts related to the natural and physical world and the understanding of naturally occurring relationships

subtopics.title: The acquisition of concepts and facts related to the natural and physical world and the understanding of naturally occurring relationships

outcomes.text: Predict, explain and infer patterns based on observations and evidence.
Articulate findings through a variety of modalities (e.g., drawings, words, dramatizations).
Recognizes familiar elements of the natural world and demonstrates an understanding that these may change over time (e.g., sun and moon, weather).
Observe and describe patterns observed over the course of a number of days and nights (e.g., differences in the activities or appearance of plants and animals).

topics.title: Pushes and pulls can have different strengths and directions, and can change the speed or direction of an object's motion or start or stop it

subtopics.title: Pushes and pulls can have different strengths and directions, and can change the speed or direction of an object's motion or start or stop it

outcomes.text: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.
Analyze data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or a pull.

topics.title: Sunlight affects the Earth's surface

subtopics.title: Sunlight affects the Earth's surface

outcomes.text: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface.
Use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area.

topics.title: To live and grow, animals obtain food they need from plants or other animals, and plants need water and light

subtopics.title: To live and grow, animals obtain food they need from plants or other animals, and plants need water and light

outcomes.text: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive.

topics.title: Patterns are observed when measuring the local weather, including how humans and other organisms impact their environment

subtopics.title: Patterns are observed when measuring the local weather, including how humans and other organisms impact their environment

outcomes.text: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.
Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals (including humans) can change the environment to meet their needs.

topics.title: Plants and animals meet their needs in their habitats and impact one another; people can prepare for severe weather

subtopics.title: Plants and animals meet their needs in their habitats and impact one another; people can prepare for severe weather

outcomes.text: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants or animals (including humans) and the places they live.
Ask questions to obtain information about the purpose of weather forecasting to prepare for, and respond to, severe weather.
Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air and/or other living things in the local environment.

topics.title: Sound can make matter vibrate and vibrating matter can make sound

subtopics.title: Sound can make matter vibrate and vibrating matter can make sound

outcomes.text: Plan and conduct investigations to provide evidence that vibrating materials can make a sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that objects can be seen only when illuminated.
Plan and conduct an investigation to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light.
Use tools and materials to design and build a device that used light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.

topics.title: All organisms have external parts that they use to perform daily functions

subtopics.title: All organisms have external parts that they use to perform daily functions

outcomes.text: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants and/or animals use their external parts to help them survive, grow and meet their needs.
Read texts and use media to determine patterns in behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.

topics.title: Young organisms are very much, but not exactly, like their parents, and also resemble other organisms of the same kind

subtopics.title: Young organisms are very much, but not exactly, like their parents, and also resemble other organisms of the same kind

outcomes.text: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.

topics.title: Patterns of movement of the sun, moon and stars as seen from Earth can be observed, described and predicted

subtopics.title: Patterns of movement of the sun, moon and stars as seen from Earth can be observed, described and predicted

outcomes.text: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.

topics.title: Matter exists as different substances that have observable different properties

subtopics.title: Matter exists as different substances that have observable different properties

outcomes.text: Plan and conduct an investigation to describe and classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.
Analyze data obtained from testing different materials to determine which materials have the properties that are best suited for an intended purpose.
Make observations to construct an evidence-based account of how an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object.
Construct an argument with evidence that some changes caused by heating or cooling can be reversed and some cannot.

topics.title: Plants depend on water and light to grow and on animals for pollination or to move their seeds around

subtopics.title: Plants depend on water and light to grow and on animals for pollination or to move their seeds around

outcomes.text: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine if plants need sunlight and water to grow.
Develop a simple model that mimics the function of an animal in dispersing seeds or pollinating plants.

topics.title: A range of different organisms lives in different places

subtopics.title: A range of different organisms lives in different places

outcomes.text: Make observations of plants and animals to compare the diversity of life in different habitats.

topics.title: Some events on Earth occur quickly; others can occur very slowly

subtopics.title: Some events on Earth occur quickly; others can occur very slowly

outcomes.text: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly or slowly.

topics.title: Wind and water can change the shape of the land; models can show the shape and these changes to the land

subtopics.title: Wind and water can change the shape of the land; models can show the shape and these changes to the land

outcomes.text: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land and bodies of water in an area.
Obtain information to identify where water is found on Earth and that it can be solid or liquid.

topics.title: Patterns of motion can be used to predict future motion

subtopics.title: Patterns of motion can be used to predict future motion

outcomes.text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.

topics.title: Objects in contact exert forces on each other; electric and magnetic forces between a pair of objects do not require contact

subtopics.title: Objects in contact exert forces on each other; electric and magnetic forces between a pair of objects do not require contact

outcomes.text: Ask questions to determine cause-and-effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.

topics.title: Organisms have unique and diverse life cycles

subtopics.title: Organisms have unique and diverse life cycles

outcomes.text: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction and death.

topics.title: Being part of a group helps animals obtain food, defend themselves and cope with changes

subtopics.title: Being part of a group helps animals obtain food, defend themselves and cope with changes

outcomes.text: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.

topics.title: Different organisms vary in how they look and function because they have different inherited information; the environment also affects the traits that an organism develops

subtopics.title: Different organisms vary in how they look and function because they have different inherited information; the environment also affects the traits that an organism develops

outcomes.text: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment

topics.title: Some living organisms resemble organisms that once lived on Earth

subtopics.title: Some living organisms resemble organisms that once lived on Earth

outcomes.text: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates and reproducing.

topics.title: Sometimes differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species provide advantages in survival and reproduction

subtopics.title: Sometimes differences in characteristics between individuals of the same species provide advantages in survival and reproduction

outcomes.text: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well and some cannot survive at all.

topics.title: Climate describes patterns of typical weather conditions over different scales and variations; historical weather patterns can be analyzed

subtopics.title: Climate describes patterns of typical weather conditions over different scales and variations; historical weather patterns can be analyzed

outcomes.text: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.

subtopics.title: A variety of weather hazards result from natural process; humans cannot eliminate weather-related hazards but can reduce their impacts

outcomes.text: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.

topics.title: The faster an object moves the more energy it has

subtopics.title: The faster an object moves the more energy it has

outcomes.text: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.

topics.title: Energy can be moved from place to place

subtopics.title: Energy can be moved from place to place

outcomes.text: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric currents.

topics.title: When objects collide contact forces transfer so as to change objects' motion

subtopics.title: When objects collide contact forces transfer so as to change objects' motion

outcomes.text: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.

topics.title: Energy can be produced, used or released by converting stored energy

subtopics.title: Energy can be produced, used or released by converting stored energy

outcomes.text: Apply scientific ideas to design, test and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.

topics.title: Waves are regular patterns of motion

subtopics.title: Waves are regular patterns of motion

outcomes.text: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.

topics.title: An object can be seen when light reflected from its surface enters the eyes

subtopics.title: An object can be seen when light reflected from its surface enters the eyes

outcomes.text: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.

topics.title: Patterns can encode, send, receive and decode information

subtopics.title: Patterns can encode, send, receive and decode information

outcomes.text: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.

topics.title: Organisms have both internal and external structures that serve various functions

subtopics.title: Organisms have both internal and external structures that serve various functions

outcomes.text: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior and reproduction.
Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information in different ways.

topics.title: Earth has changed over time

subtopics.title: Earth has changed over time

outcomes.text: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.

topics.title: Four major earth systems interact

subtopics.title: Four major earth systems interact

outcomes.text: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.

topics.title: Earth's physical features occur in patterns

subtopics.title: Earth's physical features occur in patterns

outcomes.text: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.

subtopics.title: Energy and fuels that humans use are derived from natural sources and their use affects the environment in multiple ways

outcomes.text: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.

outcomes.text: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.

topics.title: Matter exists as particles that are too small to be seen; measurements of a variety of observable properties can be used to identify particular materials

subtopics.title: Matter exists as particles that are too small to be seen; measurements of a variety of observable properties can be used to identify particular materials

subtopics.title: Chemical Reactions that occur when substances are mixed can be identified by the emergence of substances with different properties; the total mass remains the same

outcomes.text: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved.

topics.title: The gravitational force of Earth acting on an object near Earth's surface pulls that object toward the planet's center

subtopics.title: The gravitational force of Earth acting on an object near Earth's surface pulls that object toward the planet's center

outcomes.text: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.

topics.title: The energy released from food was once energy from the sun

subtopics.title: The energy released from food was once energy from the sun

outcomes.text: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for body repair, growth and motion and to maintain body warmth) was once energy from the sun.

topics.title: Plants acquire their material from growth chiefly from air and water

subtopics.title: Plants acquire their material from growth chiefly from air and water

outcomes.text: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.

topics.title: Matter cycles between air and soil and among plants, animals and microbes as these organisms live and die

subtopics.title: Matter cycles between air and soil and among plants, animals and microbes as these organisms live and die

outcomes.text: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.

outcomes.text: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky.

outcomes.text: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.

topics.title: The fact that matter is composed of atoms and molecules can be used to explain the properties of substances, diversity of materials, states of matter and phases changes

subtopics.title: The fact that matter is composed of atoms and molecules can be used to explain the properties of substances, diversity of materials, states of matter and phases changes

outcomes.text: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.
